messages:
Alex Chen: Hey team — prepping for the Acme Finance POC starting Mon. Customer SRE asked for least-privilege access for their engineers: they only need embedding generation and read-only access to logs for debugging. Also asked about expiring keys and an IP allowlist for hosted keys. Can eng confirm the recommended approach?

Priya Nair: @Alex Chen thanks — FYI Acme wants a one-week POC with a couple of SREs + 1 product engineer. We promised a secure, least-priv setup. Do we have a one-liner I can send them about what we can lock down? :thumbsup:

Jordan Lee: Short answer: yes. We can do scoped API keys + temporary expiry for hosted, and for Dedicated/Private we can provision a service account with network controls. Details: 1) Hosted API: create keys with scopes (embeddings.generate) and expiration. 2) Dedicated: create pool-specific service keys that only route to that dedicated pool. 3) Private/VPC: use customer network controls + Redwood service accounts + optional static IP egress via our gateway.

Samir Patel: Adding some nuance — currently hosted token allowlist is IP-based at the workspace level (console -> security -> IP allowlist), but we don't support per-key IP restriction yet. For per-key, recommend issuing short-lived key and enforcing from customer's side.

Lauren G.: To be concrete, here's a sample RBAC role we typically create for POCs (we can create via Console or our admin API):

```json
{
  "role": "poc_embedding_reader",
  "policies": [
    { "resource": "models:embeddings", "actions": ["generate"] },
    { "resource": "logs:read", "actions": ["list", "get"] }
  ],
  "notes": "no model fine-tune or write access; tokens expire in 7 days"
}
```

Alex Chen: That helps. Two quick questions: (1) can we tag tokens so we can bill usage to the POC separately? (2) If Acme later wants Dedicated, how disruptive is switching creds?

Jordan Lee: (1) Yes — tokens can be annotated with metadata (tags) at creation time; Console/Usage UI shows per-token breakdown. (2) We support automatic routing in the client side: you can swap to a pool-specific key and keep the same workspace objects. We can also do a canary: route 10% to Dedicated pool. Minimal app code change (replace key or endpoint).

Priya Nair: Perfect. Can someone draft the exact steps I should send to Acme SRE (they asked for a checklist)? I need to include: invite flow, role they should ask us for, how to get an expiring key, and where to put allowlist info.

Samir Patel: Draft checklist (short):
- Create Redwood workspace invite for SREs (Console -> Workspace -> Members -> Invite) and assign role `SRE (poc_embedding_reader)`.
- Request a scoped API key with scope `embeddings.generate` and set TTL=7d (we can create via Support/DevEx if they want).
- If using Hosted, add their corporate egress IPs to Workspace IP allowlist.
- For Dedicated: we create pool `acme-poc-pool-01` and issue pool-scoped key; confirm model family pinned.
- For Private/VPC: exchange allowed subnets and gateway IPs, we share onboarding checklist for VPN/peering.

Alex Chen: Nice. @InfraBot can you provision a temporary dedicated pool we can test with (small size) and post pool-id here so I can include sample config?

InfraBot: Created temporary dedicated pool `pool-acme-poc-2026` (GPU:1, region:us-west-2), expires in 14 days. Service key placeholder: `sk-prod-***-acme-poc` (create real key via Console).

Lauren G.: Alex — send me the SRE email list and I'll create the RBAC role + pre-create a 7d token they can rotate. I'll also attach a short doc snippet they can paste into their security questionnaire.

Alex Chen: Sending list now. One more — they asked if we can limit usage to embeddings only at the model family level (no text-generation). Is that enforced by role scope or by model selection?

Jordan Lee: Enforced by role scope. The `embeddings.generate` scope only allows embedding endpoints. If you attach a role that only lists that scope, attempts to call generation/model chat endpoints will be blocked. We'll enforce server-side.

Priya Nair: Great — I'll forward the checklist + ACL snippet to Acme and cc eng. Thanks everyone :rocket:

Alex Chen: Thanks! Follow-up: I might need a short blurb for the security questionnaire: can someone paste a one-paragraph answer about key expiry and least-priv access?

Lauren G.: Here's a quick blurb you can paste: "Redwood supports scoped API keys, role-based access control, and token TTLs to enforce least-privilege for short-term POCs. For hosted deployments, workspace-level IP allowlisting can further restrict access; for Dedicated and Private deployments, we provide pool-scoped keys and network isolation respectively. Tokens are auditable and can be annotated for per-POC billing. For additional controls (per-key IP restriction or HSM-bound keys) we can discuss enterprise options."

Alex Chen: Perfect — sending now. Closing this thread once Acme acknowledges.

InfraBot: Note: provisioned pool will auto-delete on 1765370000 unless extended. 

Lauren G.: I'll follow up on SSO invite cadence and thread back if anything changes. :)
